statement_comparisons.source_content: Smooth Morse–Smale dynamics on a compact manifold with finitely many critical elements; outputs preserve periodic minimal periods, separate critical points/orbit images, and satisfy rank at critical elements.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: f=0 has a continuum of nonhyperbolic equilibria. Deck-related equilibria have identical output. The dynamics and separation assumptions fail.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Real-analytic completef and real-analytich; A1nonempty compactω(x); A2observability on eachω(x); A3differentω-limit sets have different output images; A4local observability at some point of eachω(x). Conclusion: global observability on every nontrivial finite interval.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Hereω(x)={x}. A1,A2 and local A4 hold for the fixed example, butω(x)≠ω(τx) and h(ω(x))=h(ω(τx)). A3 fails. The submitted embedding is only assumed smooth, so analyticity is an additional unestablished requirement; even if granted, A3 still decisively fails.

statement_comparisons.source_content: An arbitrary complete Riemannian metric is selected as an auxiliary distance for topology/compactness; no explicit metric form is needed.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: It is not the induced observation metricP_T, and no curvature condition is imposed. Auxiliary completeness cannot supply global injectivity from observation-Gramian curvature.

statement_comparisons.source_content: ContinuousH, compactA, H injective onA and locally injective at all its points yield injectivity in a neighborhood ofA.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Assumes the global injectivity onA that it uses. On a singleton it yields a local conclusion; onA=M it already assumes the disputed global injectivity. It is not a covering obstruction from curvature.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Compact invariantA, observability onA, and local observability at a point of eachω(x) withinA; analyticity transfers interval information.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Presupposes observability onA. For singleton limit sets it yields local neighborhoods, not separation of different deck sheets.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Convergence to equilibrium/periodic critical elements, correct output period, separation of critical points/orbit images, rank.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Critical-point separationC2 fails on every deck pair. The corollary does not infer separation from curvature.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Minimal nonempty compact distalω-sets; a singleton restricted output fiber on each; A3separation and A4local observability retained.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Singleton limit sets do not remove A3. A3 again fails.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Analytic cascade; driving subsystem observable and globally asymptotically stable; zero dynamics have finitely many compact minimal/distal limit sets, noncycle condition, output singleton/separation conditions and local observability.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Zero dynamics onM have infinitely many singletonω-sets and deck-related indistinguishable output images. Relevant finite-limit/separation requirements fail.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Perspective linear flows on complex/real Grassmann/projective spaces, strong regularity and stacked matrix/polynomial rank conditions; additional rational independence for the stated real case.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: These are special matrix-induced dynamics and perspective outputs. Rank criteria ensure separation of limiting invariant subspaces. No observation-metric negative-curvature sufficiency or hyperbolic two-cover example is supplied. The remark that an unrestricted real extension is wrong concerns that matrix criterion.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Strongly regular generalized double-bracket flow on a complex Grassmannian, distinct traces at all finite equilibria and full linearized observability dimensions.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Explicit equilibrium-output separation remains. It excludes indistinguishable equilibria rather than deriving their separation from curvature.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Aeyels1982, Byrnes–Crouch1986, Crouch1981, perspective/Riccati/global-cascade/double-bracket literature and textbooks.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: No Krener/OWR curvature-conjecture reference. Their complete original sources are not all newly read here; the bibliography is not proof that those originals contain no relevant material.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Observability means every pair of initial states is distinguished by some output time. For analytic systems, the family of iterated output Lie derivatives must distinguish points. An invertible nonlinear observability matrix gives local observability.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: Every deck pair remains indistinguishable at all times. For f=0 higher Lie derivatives vanish; the family retains onlyh. LocalDh injectivity is consistent with failure of global point separation.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Linear Gramian nonsingularity characterizes linear-state recovery. Nonlinear empirical Gramian is a local approximation around a nominal trajectory. Fixed-radius constrained output difference defines a quantitative partial-observability measure in a Euclidean subspace.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: The exactP_T is positive despite distant deck collisions. The survey labels nonlinear sensitivity locally and does not assert a negative-curvature route to global injectivity. Its finite-radius optimization measure concerns larger output ambiguity directly, not curvature of the infinitesimal metric.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Linear observable/detectable pairs permit stabilizing linear error dynamics; unobservable stable modes can still be detectable.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: The fixed manifold system is nonlinear in its global observation topology, with indistinguishable constant trajectories. Linear spectral detectability is a different statement.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Nonlinear output injection and a local coordinate change around an equilibrium; displayed conditions include f(x0)=h(x0)=0 and linear dependence of iterated differential Lie derivatives. The next page explicitly confines the result to an equilibrium neighborhood.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: A local coordinate/observer construction does not recover the sheet globally. No theorem involving complete negatively curvedP_T is stated. The survey cites underlying observer results, whose original full hypotheses are not all independently re-proved or exhaustively read here.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Derivative coordinate map(1.17) is assumed a diffeomorphism on a regionΩ⊂Rn before the high-gain construction. A later discussion cites observer methods avoiding a global coordinate requirement or treating triangular/bounded nonlinear models.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: A region containing an entire indistinguishable deck pair cannot satisfy injectivity of the derivative output map. Local/structured observer results are not a universal curvature-only theorem. The actual reference is Krener–Kang2003 **Locally convergent nonlinear observers**, not a new proof of global distinguishability.

statement_comparisons.source_content: EKF/UKF, H∞ filtering, minimum-energy value functions and Hamilton–Jacobi equations; EKF convergence is generally local/unassured, noisy estimation uses specified models and optimization.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: These formulas do not establish a unique global observation inverse for the fixed two-cover or assert a curvature-conjecture resolution. The minimum-energy discussion refers to already credited Mortensen/Hijab/Krener literature.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Linear semigroup state/output operators on Hilbert spaces. Exact observability includes injectivity plus bounded inverse; approximate observability still assumes injectivity. Detectability/spectral decomposition supports suitable observers.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: A linear vector-space operator and its global norm inequality differ from the nonlinear differential Gramian on a compact hyperbolic manifold. A global coercivity inequality for all state differences is stronger thanP_T positivity at each tangent space.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Assuming appropriate inertial-manifold existence under Lipschitz/spectral conditions, long-term PDE dynamics reduce to a finite-dimensional flow; reaction-diffusion example with Neumann boundary condition is discussed.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: The attracting manifold is a graph over a vector subspace and reduction supplies dynamics, not output injectivity. No induced negatively curved observation metric or finite-sheeted hyperbolic state cover appears. This report does not endorse or extend all general PDE claims in the survey.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Observer families have different modeling/scope limits; observability is relied on for convergence.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: The conclusion assumes the needed distinguishability rather than proving it from curvature. No disposition of the OWR question is stated.

statement_comparisons.source_content: Classical observer/filter, Gramian, PDE and partial-observability works, including Hermann–Krener1977 and Krener–Ide2009.
statement_comparisons.comparison_to_fixed_counterexample: No OWR negative-curvature contribution or direct resolution appears. No new primary source among these references was full-read solely by reading this bibliography.
